# nexus piholerecord get

List local A records, or with NAME, get a local A record

Without NAME: Lists the local A records (address=/<fqdn>/<ipv4> lines) in Pi-hole's local DNS records file, with fqdn, ipv4, zone (the longest declared zone suffix, or null when unzoned), duplicate (the name has more than one A line; such a record cannot be changed until fixed by hand) and the file's etag. A record's ID is <fqdn>~A. Filter zone=<zone> or zone=unzoned. Lines Nexus does not manage are never returned. Read-only: reads the file only. Fails dependency-unavailable when the file is unreadable or larger than 1 MiB.

With NAME: Returns one local A record by its ID, <fqdn>~A, with ipv4, zone, duplicate and the file's etag. An unknown ID answers 404 not-found. Read-only: reads the file only.

## Usage

```
nexus piholerecord get [NAME] [flags]
```

## Examples

```
  # List local A records
  nexus piholerecord get
  # Get a local A record
  nexus piholerecord get <name>
```

## Flags

```
      --filter stringArray   key=value, repeatable: print only objects whose dot path has this value; a repeated key matches any of its values; the host filters by zone
  -h, --help                 help for get
  -o, --output string        output format: table, json, jsonl, yaml (default table on a terminal, jsonl otherwise)
      --select strings       print only these dot paths of each object, comma-separated, such as name,properties.state; host and id are always kept
      --stdin                read JSON Lines objects from stdin, such as another command's output, and run once per line: each binds its host and its id or name; a line without host uses the target host
      --stop-on-error        with --stdin, stop at the first line that fails
      --tag strings          target every configured host with this tag; comma-separated or repeated for any of several
```

## Global flags

```
      --host string   target hosts: configured names, comma-separated, or all (default: NEXUS_HOST, then the default host)
      --verbose       log each request and response status to stderr
```
